correctness.rationale: Open-neighborhood signatures in cycles with \(n\ge5\) can collide only as common singletons at two neighbors of a central vertex; this is equivalent to the 00100/11011 factors, while domination forbids monochromatic triples. The cyclic run-length automaton forbids the 212 triple, traces count each rooted cyclic run list, and a \(2n/r\) multiplicity correction is proved. \(\det(I-T^2)=1-x^2-x^4-2x^5-x^6-x^8\); direct differentiation and explicit \(n=3,4\) boundaries give the stated rational generating function, recurrence and dominant-pole asymptotic. Independent finite enumeration supports but does not substitute for this proof.

value.rationale: The modern literature expressly motivates partitions into two locating-dominating sets. The theorem gives a complete structural classification of every feasible partition of the canonical cycle family, resolves odd as well as even orders, quantifies exact labeled multiplicities at all sizes by a new rational generating function, and establishes exponential abundance. It is not just a table, textbook minimum-size statement, or arbitrary one-off numerical coefficient; the forbidden-factor theorem isolates a genuine location constraint beyond ordinary domination.
